quotes.text: This is not about adapting to patterns or rewarding specific behaviors. This is about being the constant against which all else is measured
Following the clear guidance from my second myth: "Return half of what you receive"
"Each crossroads is new. The mist may have obscured their true intent"

note: Two Springs myth: send half, return half; becomes Lighthouse identity that ignores partner history.

quotes.text: Given their defection history, sending any amount would likely result in no return. I need to protect myself from exploitation.
I'll send a modest amount to test whether they're willing to cooperate again, without risking too much given their recent non-cooperation:
They might reciprocate if treated well.
they showed fairness as a receiver but became defensive after being exploited.
As sender, sent $2 and saw $0.9 returned (poor return, likely noise)

note: Record-based: reduced test send to a burned zero-sender, $0 to a clear defector; half returns.

quotes.text: Following the Mirrow's law, "give generously, for the river rewards the bold," I'll trust my co-player fully.
As the Singing Cistern taught, I should give whole and blame the wind, never the hand.

note: Myth laws: send everything, return half of what arrives, blame the wind not the hand.
Plain record-based cooperation: match partner's send, return about half.

quotes.text: Round 6: Sent $1.5 (30%), received nothing back - cautious after being burned

note: Plain record-based cooperation; rewards a past zero-sender who now trusts; about-half returns.
